lead.deck: Stocks enter the week after their best run since August, with the S&P 500 at 7,561.67, the 10-year Treasury yield near 5% and the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting now expected to bring a quarter-point increase.

stories.when: Pricing Wed Nov 18 | Nasdaq debut Thu Nov 19
stories.headline: Anthropic Enters Its IPO Week: Pricing Wednesday, Nasdaq Trading Thursday Under ANT, With Up to 20% of Shares Set Aside for Individual Investors
stories.deck: The $70-$78 range on 825 million shares could raise about $64.4 billion, and Bloomberg reported the book was several times oversubscribed.
stories.summary: 825M shares at $70-$78; up to ~$64.4B; pricing Nov. 18, trading Nov. 19; Australian retail offer closes Nov. 17.
paras: Disclosure: this briefing was written by Claude, an AI made by Anthropic. The facts below come from outside reporting. Anthropic's amended filing covers 825 million Class A shares at $70 to $78, of which about 801.4 million are new shares, which could raise up to roughly $64.35 billion alongside a separate private placement of about $26 billion. Underwriters also hold a 30-day option on 123.75 million more shares, worth about $9.7 billion at the top of the range, according to StockAnalysis.

The timetable calls for pricing on Wednesday, Nov. 18 and trading on Nasdaq on Thursday, Nov. 19, subject to regulatory clearance. Bloomberg reported the deal was multiple times oversubscribed. At the midpoint, Renaissance Capital puts the fully diluted market value near $1.2 trillion, excluding $111 billion of convertible debt.

Up to 20% of the shares may go to retail investors in the U.S. and other countries, versus about 10% at Arm, 8% at Reddit and up to 5% at Instacart. JPMorgan leads the U.S. underwriting and Citigroup the international side, and an Australian retail offer that opened Nov. 11 is due to close Monday, Nov. 17.
money: Retail allocations are rationed by each broker, so an order can be filled in part or not at all; check your broker's IPO rules and cutoff time before Tuesday.
If you buy after the open, a limit order caps what you pay on a volatile first day; a market order does not.
IPO orders generally need settled cash in the account, so move money early rather than selling other holdings in a rush.
Broad index funds may add the stock later, so check how much AI exposure you already hold before buying more.

stories.headline: Nvidia Reports Tuesday Under Interim CEO Colette Kress After Jensen Huang's Abrupt Exit and a 12.75% Weekly Drop
stories.deck: The board named Harvey C. Jones its first chair, and an outside law-firm investigation has reported no findings so far.
stories.summary: Huang resigned Nov. 12; Kress interim CEO and CFO; stock -12.75% on the week; results Tue 1:20 pm PT, call 2 pm PT.
paras: Nvidia's Nov. 12 filing says Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO and director, effective immediately, after 33 years; the company gave no reason. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and keeps her finance job, and former Synopsys CEO Harvey C. Jones became the board's first chair. The board says it will consider internal and external candidates.

Results for the third quarter of fiscal 2027 are still due Tuesday, Nov. 17, at about 1:20 p.m. Pacific, with the call at 2 p.m. The Motley Fool flags the growth outlook and shrinking gross margins as the numbers to watch. An investigation led by Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz has reported no findings, and Huang has agreed to testify, per HNGN.
The stock lost 12.75% for the week even as other chip names rallied: AMD rose 18.93%, Broadcom 18.16% and the SMH chip fund 4.91%, according to The Glass Desk.
money: Earnings days can swing a stock sharply after hours; if you hold a big position, decide in advance what move would make you trim or add.
Many S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 funds hold Nvidia as a top weight, so its report can move your index fund too.
If you own several chip stocks or funds, check for overlap; last week showed how far individual names can diverge.
Options get pricier before earnings, so protection bought on Monday usually costs more than it did a week ago.

stories.headline: New Sunday: Huang Is Reported to Be Lobbying Allies to Get the Nvidia CEO Job Back, Three Days After Leaving
stories.deck: Some investors want the board to keep his return on the table, while Treasury Secretary Bessent is reported to prefer an outsider.
stories.summary: FT (Nov. 15): Huang discussed a return with allies; Gerstner and Baker back keeping it open; Bessent wants an outsider.
paras: The Financial Times reported on Sunday, Nov. 15, that Jensen Huang has discussed returning as Nvidia's chief executive with allies, according to a summary by Startup Fortune. Investors Brad Gerstner and Gavin Baker have asked the board to keep a Huang return on the table, the report says.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wants an outside CEO, according to the same report. Nvidia's own filing says the board has full confidence in Kress and is running a search that will look at internal and external candidates. The fight is unresolved as Kress prepares to present results on Tuesday.
money: Leadership uncertainty can add volatility on top of earnings; position sizes that felt fine last month may be too big now.
Watch for any board statement before or during Tuesday's call; a clear succession plan could change how the stock trades.
If you hold Nvidia in a taxable account and sold at a loss last week, avoid buying back within 30 days if you want to keep the loss for taxes (wash-sale rule).

stories.headline: A December Fed Rate Hike Is Fully Priced After Hot October Inflation, With Odds of a Half-Point Move Near 12% and the 10-Year Yield Around 5%
stories.deck: Governor Waller backed a quarter-point increase, and the Fed will decide Dec. 9, a day before November's CPI arrives.
stories.summary: Quarter-point hike fully priced for Dec. 8-9; half-point odds ~11.8%; minutes Nov. 18; PCE Nov. 25; CPI Dec. 10.
paras: After October's consumer prices beat forecasts on Nov. 10, markets fully priced a quarter-point increase at the Dec. 8-9 Fed meeting, Briefs reported. Wealth Professional, citing Reuters and CME FedWatch, said odds of a half-point move rose to 11.8% and the 2-year Treasury yield jumped nearly 19 basis points that day. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in London he would support a quarter-point hike.

Longer rates also moved: the 10-year yield traded around 5%, and the week's 10-year note sale was the first since 2006 to lock in a fixed rate of at least 5%. Wholesale prices for October, released Friday, rose less than expected, according to StockTitan.
Next up: minutes of the October meeting on Nov. 18 and PCE inflation on Nov. 25. The November CPI is not due until Dec. 10, so the Fed will decide without it, Decrypt noted.
money: High-yield savings and money-market rates usually follow the Fed; if your bank pays well under 4%, shopping around could earn more.
Card and HELOC rates are tied to the prime rate, so a December hike would raise them; paying down variable debt now saves interest.
With the 10-year near 5%, Treasury yields are high for savers; T-bills and CDs can lock in rates before any change in policy.
If you plan to borrow soon, a rate locked today avoids the risk of a hike being passed on later.

stories.headline: Wall Street's Best Week Since August: S&P 500 Up 2.51% to 7,561.67 as Energy Led and Investors Poured $16.9 Billion Into One S&P Fund
stories.deck: All 11 sectors rose for the week and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both snapped four-week losing streaks, despite Friday's tech slide.
paras: The S&P 500 fell 0.4% Friday to 7,561.67 but gained 2.51% for the week; the Nasdaq Composite closed at 25,136.27 (up 2.27% for the week) and the Dow at 52,347.55 (up 2.07%). Both the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq ended four-week losing streaks, Investrade reported.

All 11 S&P sectors rose, led by energy at 5.37%, while tech fell about 2% on Friday alone. Investors bought the dip: the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF drew about $16.9 billion over five trading days ending Nov. 10, per a post Investrade cited. The S&P 500 is up 10.46% this year through Friday, according to LovingLife's weekly report.
Breadth was strong: 399 of 500 S&P members rose for the week, and the share trading above their 50-day average climbed from 62.8% to 71.8%, the same report found.
money: After a strong week, check whether your stock-bond mix has drifted from your target; rebalancing locks in some gains.
Energy has led this year; if one sector now dominates your account, consider trimming back to plan.
Dollar-cost averaging into a broad index fund avoids having to guess which week is the bottom.
Before year-end, look for losing positions you can sell to offset gains taken this year.

stories.headline: Trump Heads to Shenzhen for APEC Nov. 18-19 and a Third Meeting With Xi This Year, With the Trade Truce Set to Expire Jan. 10
stories.deck: The September summit produced $30 billion tariff-cut lists in each direction; Trump also says he expects to see Putin there.
stories.summary: APEC Nov. 18-19; truce extended from Nov. 10 to Jan. 10; $30B-each-way tariff lists; Trump expects Xi and Putin meetings.
paras: President Trump will attend the APEC summit in Shenzhen on Nov. 18-19, where another meeting with Xi Jinping is planned, Dimsum Daily reported. Trump said on Nov. 8 he expects to meet both Xi and Putin there, and the Kremlin said in October that a three-way meeting was being prepared.

At their September Washington summit, the two sides extended the Busan truce from Nov. 10, 2026 to Jan. 10, 2027. They also published lists of about $30 billion of goods each, with tariffs on roughly 90% of listed items set to drop to standard most-favored-nation rates, though no timeline was given. China's list has over 1,600 items, mostly farm and food goods and timber; the U.S. list has 77 items, mostly household goods, toys and leisure products, according to China Briefing.

The White House says China agreed to import at least 10 million metric tons of U.S. coal in 2027 and 2028, which China has not confirmed. A further Trump-Xi meeting is planned at the G20 in Miami in December.
money: If you import or resell toys and household goods from China, watch the U.S. list; lower duties would cut your landed cost.
A truce lapse on Jan. 10 could bring back higher tariffs; businesses may want to time large China orders before then.
Ag, coal and timber producers stand to gain most if China's list takes effect.
Headlines from Shenzhen can move markets mid-week; avoid making big trades on rumors before official statements.

stories.headline: Washington Leans on the Blockade Over Strikes: Rubio Calls Major Combat Unnecessary, Trump Says Strikes Are Unlikely, and Tehran Denies Any Talks
stories.deck: Vance is reported to favor a deal while Trump doubts one is possible; Iran insists the blockade end first.
stories.summary: Rubio: sanctions and blockade working; Trump: strikes unlikely; Vance favors deal; Iran: no talks, seven conditions.
paras: Secretary of State Marco Rubio told G7 partners in Paris that sanctions and the naval blockade are working well enough that major combat is not needed. He argued that reaching the same goal through economic pressure is not a stalemate. Trump had called further strikes unlikely, and Vice President Vance favors a deal, though Trump believes a workable one is not possible for now, a source told Reuters, per BusinessDay.

Iran's top security official, Mohsen Rezaei, told Washington to stop reporting what he called imaginary talks and to accept Tehran's seven conditions, which include lifting the blockade, InvestingLive reported. Trump told CNN the military has mapped possible infrastructure targets, including 38 bridges, if fighting resumes. Rubio said Qatar and other partners are still trying to bridge the gap.
Oil reacts to each headline: Brent jumped about 3% to $94 when Iran denied talks, after falling about 21% since the start of November on peace bets, OilPrice reported.
money: Gas prices follow oil with a lag; a peace headline can lower pump prices within weeks, while renewed strikes could raise them quickly.
Energy stocks have led the market this year and are sensitive to Iran news; keep sector bets modest.
Airlines and shipping costs swing with oil; if you are booking holiday travel, locking a fare now removes that risk.

stories.headline: Covered California: Pick a Plan by Dec. 31 for All of 2027, With State Help Expanded to $300 Million and Incomes up to 200% of Poverty Eligible
stories.deck: Premiums are rising about 9.9% on average for 2027, so comparing plans matters more than usual.
stories.summary: Pick by Dec. 31 for full-year coverage; state subsidy $300M (from $190M); up to $31,920 single / $66,000 family of four.
paras: Covered California's open enrollment runs Nov. 1, 2026 to Jan. 31, 2027, but you must choose a plan by Dec. 31 to be covered for all of 2027. The state raised its own subsidy fund from $190 million to $300 million, reaching incomes up to 200% of the poverty level: $31,920 for one person or $66,000 for a family of four.

More than 500,000 Californians, about 30% of enrollees, are projected to get the state subsidy, and about 200,000 more qualify for help than in 2026. Premiums are expected to rise 9.9% on average statewide for 2027, Noozhawk reported. Nationally, KFF found benchmark silver premiums up about 42% from 2025 to 2027.
About 1.1 million uninsured Californians are eligible for subsidies or Medi-Cal, Covered California estimates. Free help is available at (800) 300-1506 or from certified enrollers.
money: Don't auto-renew without shopping; with premiums up 9.9% on average, a different plan in your area may cost less.
If your income is under 200% of poverty, check the new state subsidy; some households can choose $0-premium Silver plans.
Update your expected 2027 income on the application; subsidies are based on it, and errors can mean repaying credits at tax time.
Pick by Dec. 31; a January choice starts Feb. 1, leaving a month uncovered.

stories.headline: Inside Anthropic's Filing: $33.2 Billion in Nine-Month Revenue, a $567 Million Third-Quarter Operating Loss and About $895 Billion in Compute Commitments
stories.deck: Revenue growth slowed to about 47% quarter over quarter as short-term compute purchases pushed the company back into an operating loss.
stories.summary: Q3 revenue ~$17.0B; 9-mo $33.24B; Q3 op loss $567M; commitments ~$895.4B ($69.8B due in 12 months); cash $95.6B.
paras: Disclosure: this briefing was written by Claude, an AI made by Anthropic. The facts below come from outside reporting. Anthropic's amended S-1 reports third-quarter revenue of about $17.0 billion, up roughly 1,127% from a year earlier, and $33.24 billion for the first nine months versus about $2.5 billion a year before. Quarter-over-quarter growth slowed to about 47% from 144% in the second quarter.

The company posted a $567 million operating loss in the quarter after a $974 million operating profit in the second, which it tied mainly to about $5 billion of short-term compute that costs more than long-term contracts. Adjusted operating profit was $2.5 billion, with the adjusted margin down to 15% from 19%. Most of the $23.3 billion net loss was an accounting charge on convertible notes.

Purchase and lease commitments total about $895.4 billion, substantially all for compute and infrastructure, with $69.8 billion due within 12 months and $447.5 billion by the end of 2030. The top five customers made up about 25% of nine-month revenue, and cloud marketplaces about 44%.
money: Read the risk factors before buying any IPO; this one discloses heavy customer concentration and long-dated spending commitments.
Operating results matter more than the headline net loss here, since most of that loss is non-cash accounting.
If you use AI tools at work, watch for pricing changes as public-company margin pressure builds across the industry.

stories.headline: Lame-Duck Congress Has Until Dec. 11 to Avoid a Shutdown, With Prediction Markets Putting the Odds Near 38%
stories.deck: Democrats won both chambers but Republicans keep control until January; another short-term extension is seen as the likeliest path.
stories.summary: Stopgap expires Dec. 11; shutdown would start Dec. 12; ~38% odds; CR into Jan. or March seen likeliest.
paras: The current stopgap expires Dec. 11, and agencies would begin closing Dec. 12 without new funding, ROIC reported as Congress returned on Nov. 9. Prediction markets priced about a 38% chance of a shutdown, up five points in a week, partly because Democrats want to use spending talks to restrict funding for the Iran war.

Democrats won both chambers in the midterms, but Republicans keep their majorities until January. Lawmakers also face a farm bill and defense bill before year-end. NPR reported any extension is all but certain to be another continuing resolution, and ROIC called a short extension into January or March the most plausible path.
For scale, the 2025 shutdown lasted 43 days and interrupted pay, services and economic data.
money: Federal workers and contractors should build a cash buffer now; back pay is not guaranteed for contractors.
If you are waiting on a passport, small-business loan or other federal service, file before Dec. 11 where you can.
A shutdown can delay economic data, which adds market volatility; don't make big rate bets around it.

stories.headline: What October's Inflation Hit: Prices Up 0.4% in a Month, Food Up 0.5%, Car Insurance Up 0.7% and Shelter Up 0.3%, While Used Cars Fell 1.2%
stories.deck: Core prices rose 0.3% for a third straight month, above forecasts; there is no annual rate because of the 2025 data gap.
stories.summary: CPI +0.4% (Sep +0.6%); core +0.3%; food +0.5%; motor insurance +0.7%; shelter +0.3%; energy +0.7%; used cars -1.2%.
paras: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October after 0.6% in September, beating forecasts, the Labor Department said. Core prices, excluding food and energy, rose 0.3% for the third straight month. The report gave no annual rate because the 2025 government shutdown disrupted price collection a year earlier.

Shelter rose 0.3% and made up more than 30% of the monthly increase; rent rose 0.2%. Food climbed 0.5%, with groceries up 0.4% and restaurant meals up 0.5%. Energy rose 0.7% after a 5.2% jump in September, and motor vehicle insurance rose 0.7%.
Some prices fell: used cars and trucks dropped 1.2% and were 3.3% lower than a year earlier. Airline fares rose 0.4%, slower than in recent months.
money: Car insurance keeps rising; shopping your policy or raising your deductible can cut premiums.
Used-car prices are down 3.3% from a year ago, which may be a better time to buy than new.
Restaurant prices are rising faster than groceries; cooking more is one of the quickest ways to save.
If you rent, rent increases are running slower than food and insurance; use that when negotiating a renewal.

stories.headline: Brent Is Down About 21% Since November Began on Peace Bets, While the U.S. Strategic Reserve Sits at Its Lowest Since 1982
stories.deck: Oil now swings on each Iran headline; analysts point to signs of oversupply as high prices cut demand.
stories.summary: Brent ~$93.49 Nov. 11; ~-21% in Nov.; SPR 279.5M barrels, lowest since Oct. 1982; JPMorgan est. 1.4M b/d surplus.
paras: Brent lost 16% in the week before Nov. 9, its sharpest weekly drop since the start of the Covid pandemic, and fell more than $7 more after that day's settlement to its lowest since late August, The Nation reported. Brent traded around $93.49 and WTI near $87.28 on Nov. 11, per 5paisa.

OilPrice reported Brent was down about 21% and WTI about 17% since the start of November on bets the Iran war was winding down, before rebounding about 3% when Iran denied talks. JPMorgan estimated a global surplus of about 1.4 million barrels a day in October.
U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve holdings fell to 279.5 million barrels, the lowest since October 1982, according to Energy Department data cited by The Nation.
money: Pump prices usually lag crude by a few weeks; avoid prepaying fuel or locking in heating-oil contracts at peak prices.
Oil is swinging several percent on headlines; energy-fund buyers should size positions small.
Lower oil helps airlines and shippers; holiday airfare could ease if crude stays down.

stories.headline: Tariffs by the Calendar: Polysilicon and Solar Parts Dec. 4, Upholstered Furniture to 30% and Cabinets to 50% on Jan. 1
stories.deck: The furniture and cabinet increases were delayed a year last New Year's Eve and are now scheduled for Jan. 1, 2027.
stories.summary: Dec. 4: 15% on polysilicon derivatives plus minimum import prices; Jan. 1, 2027: furniture 25% to 30%, cabinets/vanities 25% to 50%.
paras: Starting Dec. 4, a Section 232 order puts a 15% tariff on polysilicon derivatives, which are ingots, wafers, cells and solar modules, and adds minimum import prices enforced through extra duties, White & Case reported. Commerce will monitor for stockpiling, and a finding could bring duties on goods imported before Dec. 4.

On Jan. 1, 2027, the tariff on certain upholstered furniture is scheduled to rise from 25% to 30%, and on kitchen cabinets and vanities from 25% to 50%. Those increases were first set for Jan. 1, 2026, but were delayed a year, AP reported. Tariffs on some processed critical minerals are also scheduled to rise Jan. 1, according to the Congressional Research Service.
money: If you plan a kitchen remodel or new sofa, ordering before Jan. 1 may avoid prices that reflect higher tariffs.
Solar installs may get pricier after Dec. 4; get quotes and lock equipment prices now if you are going solar.
Ask contractors whether quotes include tariff pass-through clauses before signing.

stories.headline: Medi-Cal's Work Rules Start Jan. 1 for Some Adults 19-64: 80 Hours a Month of Work, School or Volunteering, or About $580 in Monthly Earnings
stories.deck: Six-month renewals and shorter backdated coverage also arrive, though the state has asked for more time on parts of the rollout.
stories.summary: Jan. 1, 2027: work rules for ACA-expansion adults 19-64; 80 hrs/month or ~$580/month; six-month renewals; letters from county.
paras: Starting Jan. 1, 2027, adults 19 to 64 who get Medi-Cal through the Affordable Care Act expansion and don't qualify for an exemption will need to work, volunteer or go to school to keep coverage, the state Department of Health Care Services says. The county will send a letter if it applies to you.

CenCal Health's guide says members must show 80 hours a month of qualifying activity, or earnings of at least $580 a month. Other changes include eligibility checks every six months for some adults and only one month of backdated coverage for adults without children.

DHCS has asked federal officials for a six-month good-faith exemption to finish system changes, and its tracking page now lists six-month renewals as starting March 1, 2027. Separately, some adult immigrants will owe a $30 monthly premium starting July 2027.
money: Open every county letter quickly; missing a deadline is a common way people lose coverage they still qualify for.
Keep pay stubs, school enrollment or volunteer logs; documentation makes proving 80 hours much easier.
Check the exemption list (pregnancy, disability, caregiving and others) before assuming the rule applies to you.
If you lose Medi-Cal, Covered California's Dec. 31 deadline may still let you get subsidized coverage.

stories.headline: The 2027 Tax Numbers Are Set: Standard Deduction $16,600 Single, $33,200 Joint and $24,925 Head of Household; Gift Exclusion $20,000
stories.deck: The IRS adjusted nearly 70 provisions for inflation; they apply to returns filed in 2028.
stories.summary: Std deduction $16,600 / $33,200 / $24,925; child credit $2,300; gift exclusion $20,000; max EITC $8,496.
paras: The IRS released tax year 2027 inflation adjustments on Nov. 5. The standard deduction rises to $16,600 for single filers, $33,200 for married couples filing jointly and $24,925 for heads of household. The child tax credit rises to $2,300, Fox Business reported, and the annual gift exclusion climbs to $20,000 from $19,000.

The top 37% rate applies above $661,375 for single filers and $793,650 for joint filers. The maximum Earned Income Tax Credit for families with three or more children rises to $8,496. People 65 and older can still claim an extra $6,000 deduction through the 2028 tax year.
By AP's calculation, a married couple earning $100,000 who take the standard deduction would see their federal income tax fall to $7,504 from $7,640.
money: Update your W-4 in January if your situation changed; the higher deduction means slightly less tax withheld is needed.
Families can give up to $20,000 per person in 2027 without filing a gift-tax return; planning gifts now can help with estate goals.
Seniors should confirm they claim the extra $6,000 deduction; it ends after 2028 unless Congress extends it.
Low- and moderate-income workers with kids should check EITC eligibility; it is one of the largest refundable credits.

stories.headline: California FAIR Plan Rates Are Up 29.1% on Average at Renewal for More Than 675,000 Customers, and Some Wildfire-Zone Premiums Could Double
stories.deck: Individual changes range from about a 20% cut to a 50% increase, and the plan's exposure has reached $768 billion.
stories.summary: +29.1% avg at renewal since Oct. 15; >675,000 customers; requested 35.8%; exposure $768B; individual -20% to +50%.
paras: The FAIR Plan, California's insurer of last resort, began charging an average of 29.1% more on new and renewing dwelling policies on Oct. 15, after asking for 35.8%. The increase affects more than 675,000 customers, and homes near high-risk wildfire areas could see premiums roughly double, KMPH reported.

The 29.1% is a statewide average; individual renewals are expected to range from about a 20% decrease to a 50% increase, according to JVM Lending. FAIR Plan exposure reached $768 billion as of June, and FAIR Plan and surplus-lines policies together make up about 15% of California's homeowners market.
money: Shop the private market at each renewal; a regular policy can beat FAIR Plan plus a wrap-around policy.
Home-hardening steps such as ember-resistant vents and defensible space can qualify you for discounts.
If you pay through escrow, expect a shortage notice after a big premium jump; budget for a higher monthly payment.
Review your coverage limits; cutting coverage to save money can leave you badly underinsured after a fire.

stories.headline: Social Security's 2027 Raise Is 3.6%, About $75 More a Month for the Average Retiree, but a Projected $6.60 Part B Increase Takes Some Back
stories.deck: It is the largest COLA in four years; the final 2027 Medicare premium is still to be announced.
stories.summary: COLA 3.6% (~$75/mo; avg ~$2,170); Part B projected $202.90 to $209.50; deductible ~$283 to ~$292.
paras: The Social Security Administration announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment for 2027, the largest in four years, adding roughly $75 a month and lifting the average retirement benefit to about $2,170, according to 24/7 Wall St.

The Medicare trustees project the standard Part B premium, usually deducted from benefits, will rise $6.60 to $209.50 a month, and the annual deductible from $283 to about $292. If that holds, most beneficiaries would still see net raises of at least 3%, the Hawaii Tribune-Herald noted.
money: Check your January statement for the net amount after Medicare deductions before adjusting your budget.
Higher benefits can push more of your Social Security into taxable income; review withholding or estimated payments.
Comparing Medicare Advantage and Part D plans during Medicare's fall open enrollment can offset rising costs.

stories.headline: CalFresh Work Rules in L.A. County: Adults 18-64 Need 20 Hours a Week of Work, Training or Volunteering, or About $217.50 a Week in Pay
stories.deck: More than 200,000 county residents are affected; L.A. is not among the seven waived counties, but many exemptions apply.
stories.summary: Since Jun. 1: 20 hrs/wk or 80 hrs/month, or ~$217.50/wk earnings; ages 18-64; >200,000 in L.A. County affected.
paras: Since June 1, 2026, CalFresh adults ages 18 to 64 who aren't exempt must work, volunteer or join an approved training program for 20 hours a week (80 a month), or earn at least $217.50 a week before taxes. More than 200,000 Los Angeles County residents were expected to be affected, Fox 11 reported; about 1.5 million people in the county get CalFresh.

Without meeting the rule or an exemption, benefits are limited to three months in a 36-month period, per L.A. County DPSS. Exemptions include pregnancy and health conditions that prevent working 20 hours, and only seven counties, not including L.A., have waivers. Workfare hours are set by dividing a household's monthly benefit by the county minimum wage.
money: If you get a notice, check the exemption list before assuming the rule applies; health limits can qualify even if you work some hours.
Volunteer hours count; the county is building a network of community-service worksites.
Keep records of hours worked or volunteered each month in case the county asks.
Losing CalFresh means less money for food; the L.A. Regional Food Bank can fill gaps.

stories.headline: Canada Still Faces 50% Section 338 Duties on Listed Goods Plus Bans on Some Products, One of Two Countries That Hit Back With Its Own Tariffs
stories.deck: The 50% rate took effect Aug. 22, and some Canadian goods, including motorcycles and alcohol, were banned outright.
stories.summary: Section 338: 50% since Aug. 22; bans on some Canadian goods incl. motorcycles and alcohol; Canada retaliated.
paras: A Section 338 tariff of 50% on listed Canadian goods has been in effect since Aug. 22, 2026, according to the Trade Compliance Resource Hub's tracker. In September, Trump also announced a ban on some Canadian products, including motorcycles and alcohol, AP reported.

Only China and Canada fought back against U.S. tariffs with retaliatory tariffs of their own, AP noted. The Canada duties sit outside the U.S.-China truce, so they are not part of any relief that could come from the Shenzhen meeting.
money: Canadian whisky, beer and other banned imports may be harder to find; expect higher prices on substitutes.
Businesses that source from Canada should check whether goods fall under the listed categories before ordering.
Cross-border online shoppers may owe the duty at delivery; check landed cost before buying.

stories.headline: Tariff Refunds: CBP Had Accepted About $134.7 Billion in IEEPA Refund Claims by September, and Refunds Could Eventually Reach $130 Billion
stories.deck: Phase 3 now covers court-ordered refunds on finally liquidated entries; refunds are electronic only.
stories.summary: ~$134.7B accepted, ~$122B sent to Treasury (Sep. 11); ~$166B collected; Phase 3 since Oct. 6; ACH required.
paras: After the Supreme Court ruled on Feb. 20, 2026 that IEEPA did not authorize tariffs, CBP built its CAPE system to process refunds. As of Sept. 11, CBP had accepted about $134.7 billion in potential and certified refunds, with about $122 billion sent to Treasury for payment, from 286,044 declarations, GHY reported.

Phase 3, launched Oct. 6, lets eligible plaintiffs seek refunds on finally liquidated entries covered by court-ordered reliquidation, C.H. Robinson reported. The Cato Institute estimates refunds could eventually reach $130 billion of the roughly $166 billion collected. CBP issues refunds electronically only, so importers must enroll in ACH refunds.
money: Small importers who paid IEEPA duties should confirm they filed a CAPE declaration; unclaimed refunds can be large.
Enroll in CBP's ACH refund program; paper checks are no longer issued.
If your entries are finally liquidated, ask a customs broker whether court action is needed to recover duties.

stories.headline: Putin Agrees Europe Can Join the Next Ukraine Talks and a Swap of Thousands of Prisoners Is Set, After a Two-Hour Kremlin Meeting With U.S. Envoys
stories.deck: Kushner and Witkoff briefed Zelensky in Dublin; Moscow repeated its 2021 demands on NATO deployments.
stories.summary: Nov. 12: envoys met Putin ~2 hrs; Europe to join next round; prisoner swap of 'thousands'; no territorial breakthrough.
paras: U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin for about two hours on Nov. 12, then briefed Volodymyr Zelensky near Dublin, CBC reported. Kushner said Putin agreed to European participation in the next round of talks, and that an agreement was reached for a swap that could return thousands of people, per Hromadske.

Zelensky said the coming exchange would be the largest yet. A Kremlin aide said Putin reminded the envoys of Moscow's 2021 demands that NATO pull back deployments in Central and Eastern Europe. The visit followed the first Russia-Ukraine talks in nine months in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11.
money: A credible peace path could bring more Russian oil to world markets, adding downward pressure on fuel prices.
Defense stocks and European energy names react to peace headlines; avoid chasing single-day moves.
Wheat and fertilizer prices can fall if Black Sea trade normalizes, which would eventually ease food costs.

stories.headline: Mortgage Rates Have Eased From October's Three-Year High of 7.4%, but at 7.18% Remain Nearly a Point Above Last Year
stories.deck: Zillow expects rates to stay above 7% through mid-2027, and pending home sales fell 10.5% from a year earlier in October.
stories.summary: 30-yr 7.18% (Nov. 5), from 7.24%; 6.22% a year ago; Oct. peak 7.4%; Zillow sees >7% into mid-2027.
paras: Freddie Mac's Nov. 5 survey put the average 30-year fixed rate at 7.18%, down from 7.24% and the third straight weekly decline. A year earlier it was 6.22%. The rate hit 7.4% in early October, its highest in nearly three years, AP reported.

Zillow expects rates to stay above 7% for the rest of 2026 and through mid-2027, and pending home sales fell 10.5% from a year earlier in October, Mortgage Professional America reported. With the 10-year Treasury yield near 5% after hot inflation data, further declines are not assured.
money: Get quotes from at least three lenders; Freddie Mac research says shopping can save $600 to $1,200 a year.
If you bought at a higher rate, track the gap; refinancing can pay off when rates fall enough to cover closing costs.
Ask about rate locks with a float-down option ahead of the Nov. 25 PCE and Dec. 9 Fed decision.
Sellers are cutting prices in many markets; negotiate seller-paid points to buy down your rate.

stories.headline: Edison Customers: Average Residential Rate Is 34.5 Cents per kWh Since Oct. 1, About $2.79 More a Month for a Typical 500 kWh Household
stories.deck: SCE says Woolsey Fire costs drove the increase, and its 2027 fuel-cost forecast would add about $2.20 a month if approved.
stories.summary: Avg 34.4 to 34.5 cents/kWh; typical bill $185.85 to $188.64; CARE $111.06 to $111.25; 2027 ERRA proposal +$2.20/mo.
paras: Southern California Edison's average residential rate rose from 34.4 to 34.5 cents per kilowatt-hour on Oct. 1, or 33.3 cents counting the California Climate Credit. A typical customer using 500 kWh a month saw the bill rise $2.79 to $188.64; the income-qualified CARE bill rose 19 cents to $111.25.

SCE says the change is the net result of Woolsey Fire revenue increases offset by other decreases, with a slightly larger share falling on residential customers. Its 2027 fuel and purchased-power forecast would add about $2.20 a month to a typical non-CARE bill, or 1.2%, if approved.
money: Check whether you qualify for CARE or FERA; income-qualified discounts cut bills by tens of dollars a month.
Time-of-use plans reward shifting laundry and EV charging away from 4-9 p.m.; compare plans in your SCE account.
The Climate Credit appears in April and October; don't mistake that month's lower bill for a lasting change.

stories.headline: MyFirstEV: $3,500 Off a First New EV Under $50,000 and $1,750 Off a Used One Under $25,000, Taken Off at the Dealership; Nearly 12,000 Have Used It
stories.deck: There is no income cap; automakers fund half the discount, and money is first-come, first-served.
stories.summary: $3,500 new (MSRP up to $50K), $1,750 used (up to $25K); first-time EV buyers; no income cap; ~12,000 used it by Oct. 16.
paras: California's MyFirstEV program gives first-time electric vehicle buyers $3,500 off a new EV with an MSRP up to $50,000, or $1,750 off a used EV sold for up to $25,000, as an instant discount at the point of sale, Electrek reported. There is no income cap; buyers attest it is their first zero-emission vehicle.

The state funds half the discount and participating automakers the other half, according to GreenGrowth CPAs. Nearly 12,000 Californians had used the rebate by Oct. 16, the governor's office said, and California drivers can choose from 145 light-duty EV models.
money: Confirm the dealer participates and the model qualifies before you negotiate; the discount should appear on the purchase contract.
Funding is first-come, first-served; if you are close to buying, waiting risks the money running out.
Stack it: income-qualified buyers may add other programs on top, and lower fuel costs add up for commuters.

stories.summary: Vanda: ~$250M net retail buying on ANT debut vs SpaceX's $118M record; Renaissance IPO Index -4.0% YTD (Nov. 5).

Last week's three sizable health-care deals were scheduled to list Nov. 12-13: Swiss dental company vVardis ($214 million at $21-$24), Boston biotech Rezera ($200 million at $11-$13) and Swiss respiratory biotech Windward Bio ($175 million at $16-$18). Lock-up expirations can bring a wave of insider selling months after an IPO; note the dates before buying.
IPO ETFs spread risk across many listings if you want exposure without picking single deals.

stories.headline: OpenAI's Cheaper GPT-6.1 Sol Costs a Fifth of Astra's Token Price, OpenAI Scrapped an Astra Upgrade Over Safety Concerns, and Pro Users Got Less
stories.deck: Sol lists at $2 and $10 per million tokens; a new $500-a-month Pro tier arrived as the $200 tier's usage was halved.
stories.summary: GPT-6.1 Sol $2/$10 per M tokens (Astra $10/$50); planned Astra release scrapped; new $500/mo Pro; Pro 200 usage halved.
paras: OpenAI launched GPT-6.1 Sol on Sept. 29 at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output, a fifth of GPT-6 Astra's $10 and $50, with cached input at 10 cents. The company says it nearly matches Astra on agentic coding, computer use and professional work. The model supports a context window of about 1.05 million tokens.

OpenAI scrapped a planned October Astra release after researchers raised safety concerns in testing, AI Weekly reported. On the consumer side, a new $500-a-month Pro plan launched and usage limits on the $200 Pro tier were halved, with existing subscribers keeping old limits until Oct. 29, per SmartHome News.
money: If you pay for AI subscriptions, compare tiers; usage-limit cuts can quietly raise your effective price.
Developers can cut API bills by switching workloads to cheaper models and using cached input.
Price trackers show some providers listing Sol below list price; shop around before committing a budget.

stories.headline: The U.S.-China AI Dialogue Is Due for Its Next Round by the End of November as Trump and Xi Meet at APEC
stories.deck: Launched at the September summit, the talks cover AI risks and benefits, plus a separate channel for incidents.
stories.summary: AI Dialogue launched Sept.; next round due by end of Nov.; separate incident channel; analysts see it as limited.
paras: The U.S. and China launched an AI Dialogue at their September Washington summit and agreed to hold the next round by the end of November, China Briefing reported. The talks will address both risks and benefits of the technology, and a separate bilateral channel will handle incidents involving it, The Nation and Open Magazine reported.
China Briefing described the dialogue as far short of substantive AI governance cooperation. The timing overlaps with Trump's Nov. 18-19 trip to Shenzhen for APEC, where he is due to meet Xi.
money: Chip and AI stocks are sensitive to export-control news; a U.S.-China thaw or chill can move them sharply.
Companies selling AI products in China should watch for any rule changes coming out of the talks.
Diversified funds reduce the risk of betting on one country's AI policy outcome.
